reason: The passage describes Yahweh taking deliberate action to preserve and deliver the Israelites to safety: He instructs them to advance, parts the Red Sea to provide an escape route, protects them with walls of water on both sides, and destroys the pursuing Egyptian army. These actions demonstrate protective care for the Israelites' welfare and preservation. While the text emphasizes that these acts serve Yahweh's glorification (וְאִכָּבְדָ֤ה בְּפַרְעֹה - 'I will be glorified in Pharaoh'), the practical outcome is their deliverance from mortal danger and their safe passage to the other side. In the biblical narrative context, God's glorification through saving His covenant people is consistent with wanting their well-being.
story: The Parting of the Red Sea
